authors_full: Dhruv Agarwal, Mor Naaman, Aditya Vashistha
title: AI Suggestions Homogenize Writing Toward Western Styles and Diminish Cultural Nuances
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '25), Yokohama, Japan, April 26-May 1, 2025, ACM
pdf_filename: Agarwal Naaman Vashistha (2025) - AI Suggestions Homogenize Writing Toward Western Styles and Diminish Cultural Nu.pdf
one_line_finding: Random assignment to GPT-4o inline suggestions raised the mean cosine similarity between Indian and American essays from 0.48 (SD 0.11) to 0.54 (SD 0.13), t(6958) = −17.89, p < 0.001, d = −0.44 over essay pairs (pp. 9-10, Section 4.3.1), and lowered a classifier's accuracy at telling Indian from American essays from 90.6% to 83.5%, t(38) = 2.25, p = 0.03, d = 0.71 (p. 10, Section 4.3.2).

authors_full: Mustafa Akben, Jacob Carignan, Manuel Anyimah
title: The Confidence Cage: How Creative Self-Efficacy Hinders Gen AI-Augmented Ideation
venue: Proceedings of the 59th Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences
pdf_filename: Akben Carignan Anyimah (2026) - The Confidence Cage.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 300 analyzed participants, GPT-4o coaching increased automated AUT creativity versus web search (unadjusted M = 3.21 versus 2.98; reported d = 0.77), but adjusted arm labels conflict between the results prose and Table 2 (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1; p. 5, Section 4; p. 6, Table 2).

authors_full: Joshua Ashkinaze, Julia Mendelsohn, Li Qiwei, Ceren Budak, Eric Gilbert
title: How AI Ideas Affect the Creativity, Diversity, and Evolution of Human Ideas: Evidence From a Large, Dynamic Experiment
venue: Proceedings of the ACM Collective Intelligence Conference (CI 2025), San Diego, CA, USA, August 4-6, 2025 (ACM)
pdf_filename: Ashkinaze et al (2025) - How AI Ideas Affect Creativity Diversity Evolution.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 844 online volunteers analyzed (3,414 AUT ideas analyzed), seeing ChatGPT example ideas did not change classifier-scored originality (joint F(4, 19.86) = 0.12, p = 0.97; p. 8, Section 5.4; per-arm coefficients in Table 18, p. 26), but both high-exposure conditions raised global idea diversity over the human-examples control (Cliff's delta 0.31 disclosed and 0.26 undisclosed, adjusted p = 0.001; p. 7, Section 5.2; Table 12, p. 22).

authors_full: Hemanth Asirvatham, Chiara Betti, Rachel Brown, Arnaldo Camuffo, Aaron Chatterji, Chiara Fumagalli, Alfonso Gambardella, Myriam Mariani, Abhinav Pandey, Steve Ramos, Giovanni Salvucci, Vladimir Simic
title: Training Novices to Think, or Giving Them LLMs? Evidence from an RCT
pdf_filename: Asirvatham et al (2026) - Training Novices to Think, or Giving Them LLMs.pdf
one_line_finding: ChatGPT increased recommendation usefulness by 0.862 points (SE 0.079) and idea count by 2.251 (SE 0.290), with no clear effect on between-person diversity (-0.002, SE 0.002); causal training increased diversity by 0.018 (SE 0.003) (Tables A.10 and A.12, PDF pp. 45-46).

authors_full: Federico Atzori, Luca Corazzini, Valeria Maggian, Filippo Pavesi, Massimo Scotti
title: Human-AI Interaction in Creative Tasks: an Experimental Investigation
venue: Working Papers, Department of Economics, Ca' Foscari University of Venice
pdf_filename: Atzori et al (2026) - Human-AI Interaction in Creative Tasks.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 360 analyzed participants, mostly students, ChatGPT access increased mean rated creativity by 0.398 points (robust SE 0.139; PDF p. 23, Table 5, column 1).

authors_full: Rosó Baltà-Salvador, Ismail El-Madafri, Enric Brasó-Vives, Marta Peña
title: Empowering Engineering Students Through Artificial Intelligence (AI): Blended Human–AI Creative Ideation Processes With ChatGPT
pdf_filename: Balta-Salvador El-Madafri Braso-Vives Pena (2025) - Empowering Engineering Students Through Artificial Intelligence (AI).pdf
one_line_finding: Among 51 analyzed students who produced 728 ideas, ChatGPT assistance showed no significant peer-rated differences, while an observational prior-experience comparison found higher overall scores for experienced users (3.00 [SD 0.82] versus 2.75 [SD 0.94], p = 0.039; p. 16, Section 7; p. 7, Table 3; p. 9, Section 5; p. 11, Figure 7 and Table 4).

authors_full: Rosó Baltà-Salvador, Enric Brasó-Vives, Marta Peña
title: Evaluating AI-assisted creative ideation: A crossover study in higher education
pdf_filename: Balta-Salvador Braso-Vives Pena (2026) - Evaluating AI-assisted creative ideation.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 51 analyzed students, pooled within-person comparisons found more Existing Solutions with ChatGPT (1.00 vs 0.55, p = .011) and shorter descriptions (23.36 vs 25.57 words, p = .015), with no statistically significant differences in fluency, flexibility, or originality (p. 8, Table 4); thematic diversity was comparable (p. 10, Table 7 and Section 4.3), while semantic divergence was printed as higher with AI (0.29 vs 0.28) despite the narrative describing it as lower (p. 10, Section 4.3).

authors_full: Mia Magdalena Bangerl, Leonie Disch, Tamara David, Viktoria Pammer-Schindler
title: CreAItive Collaboration? Users' Misjudgment of AI-Creativity Affects Their Collaborative Performance
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI 2025), ACM
pdf_filename: Bangerl et al (2025) - CreAItive Collaboration.pdf
one_line_finding: The paper reports no significant main-test differences in AUT fluency (14.6 vs 12.7), originality (3.7 vs 3.7), or flexibility (10.0 vs 9.4), but lower AI-group elaboration immediately (2.1 vs 3.8; U = 924.0, p = 0.005) and after AI removal (2.8 vs 4.7; U = 970.0, p = 0.012), with no significant retention difference three weeks later (1.9 vs 2.2), although the elaboration tests have unresolved analysis units (pp. 8-10, Sections 5.1.1-5.1.3 and Figures 4, 8, 12).

authors_full: Connor Baumler, Calvin Bao, Huy Nghiem, Xinchen Yang, Marine Carpuat, Hal Daumé III
title: Can You Make It Sound Like You? Post-Editing LLM-Generated Text for Personal Style
venue: Proceedings of the 64th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
pdf_filename: Baumler et al (2026) - Can You Make It Sound Like You.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 81 analyzed writers, post-edited AI drafts were less stylistically diverse than unassisted writing (similarity Hedges’ g = 1.42, 95% CI [1.33, 1.51], p = .0002; sample: p. 13, Appendix A.1; result: p. 6, section 6.2 and p. 16, Table 3, H2a).

authors_full: Yixuan Chen, Xuemei Wu, Yihua Zhong, Changqin Huang
title: Effects of Personalized Generative AI on Student Creativity: Evidence from Creative Performance, Self-efficacy, and Attention Allocation
venue: Technology in Education. Smart and Innovative Learning (ICTE 2025), Communications in Computer and Information Science (Springer Nature Singapore)
pdf_filename: Chen et al (2025) - Effects of Personalized Generative AI on Student Creativity.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 62 analyzed students, personalized GPT-4 feedback produced higher rated quality (3.50 vs 3.08, p = .001, r = .42) and elaboration (3.58 vs 2.48, p < .001, r = .62) than standard ChatGPT-4, with no significant originality difference (2.92 vs 3.13, p = .098, r = .18), using the values printed in c041 (PDF p. 8, printed p. 383, Sect. 4.1; Fig. 4A).

authors_full: Yixuan Chen, Changqin Huang, Zhongmei Han, Di Zhang, Yiheng Lou, Yihua Zhong
title: Investigating student engagement with personalised generative AI feedback: Effects on creative problem-solving and feedback uptake
pdf_filename: Chen et al (2026) - Investigating student engagement with personalised generative AI feedback.pdf
one_line_finding: Personalised versus standard GenAI feedback yielded higher solution quality (3.50 vs 3.08, p = .001) and elaboration (3.58 vs 2.48, p < .001), with no clear originality difference (2.92 vs 3.13, p = 0.098; PDF p. 11, printed p. 175, Table 2).

authors_full: Xusen Cheng, Lulu Zhang
title: Inspiration booster or creative fixation? The dual mechanisms of LLMs in shaping individual creativity in tasks of different complexity
pdf_filename: Cheng et al (2025) - Inspiration booster or creative fixation.pdf
one_line_finding: With 204 people analyzed per experiment, an LLM partner posting ERNIE Bot ideas raised expert-rated creativity over a scripted human partner on the simple task (2.549 vs 2.182, F(1,200) = 17.152, P < 0.001) and scored lower on the complex task (2.351 vs 2.441, F(1,200) = 1.021, printed with P = 0.028), while two ideas per response instead of ten raised complex-task creativity (2.520 vs 2.139) and lowered simple-task creativity (2.171 vs 2.466) (pp. 5 and 7).

authors_full: Vanja Čok, Damien Motte, Khadija Hmina, Ibtissam El Hassani, Ivan Demšar, Jože Tavčar, Nikola Vukašinović
title: Evaluating TRIZ with and without LLM support: an experimental study on engineering problem-solving
pdf_filename: Cok et al (2026) - Evaluating TRIZ with and without LLM support.pdf
one_line_finding: In a two-way ANOVA of expert-rated design quality (1-7), the LLM's main effect across the three problems was not significant (F(1, 108) = 3.21, p = .076), and method interacted with problem (F(2, 108) = 7.58, p = .001): the LLM raised quality on the general WT problem (6.2 vs 5.0, F(1, 108) = 34.67, p < .001) but not on the specialized GT (4.6 vs 4.9, p = .479) or MB (4.2 vs 4.2, p = .809) problems (p. 512, Section 4.2 and Table 2).

authors_full: Zara Contractor, Germán Reyes
title: Experimental Evidence on the Learning Impact of Generative AI
pdf_filename: Contractor & Reyes (2026-09) - AI Learning RCT.pdf
one_line_finding: AI access showed no detectable change in between-student essay similarity during access (coefficient 0.001, SE 0.007; control mean 0.774) or one week later without AI (-0.005, SE 0.013; control mean 0.762; p. 39, Table 5 Panel C).

authors_full: Fabrizio Dell'Acqua, Edward McFowland III, Ethan Mollick, Hila Lifshitz, Katherine C. Kellogg, Saran Rajendran, Lisa Krayer, François Candelon, Karim R. Lakhani
title: Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier: Field Experimental Evidence of the Effects of Artificial Intelligence on Knowledge Worker Productivity and Quality
pdf_filename: Dell'Acqua et al (2026) - Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 385 BCG consultants analyzed in the shoe-product experiment, GPT-4 access raised the human-graded composite quality score by 1.556 (SE 0.080, GPT Only) and 1.746 (SE 0.074, GPT + Overview) over a control mean of 4.099 (PDF p. 38, Table 1), while the across-subject similarity of their shoe ideas was higher in both AI arms than in the control arm, shown only as density plots with no statistics (PDF p. 36, Figure 6).

authors_full: Fabrizio Dell'Acqua, Charles Ayoubi, Hila Lifshitz, Raffaella Sadun, Ethan Mollick, Lilach Mollick, Yi Han, Jeff Goldman, Hari Nair, Stew Taub, Karim R. Lakhani
title: The Cybernetic Teammate: A Field Experiment on Generative AI and Teamwork
pdf_filename: Dell'Acqua et al (2026) - The Cybernetic Teammate.pdf
one_line_finding: Individuals randomly assigned a GPT-4-based tool produced solutions rated 0.373 control-group SD higher in overall quality than individuals without AI (SE 0.106; Table 2, p. 42), about the level of two-person teams without AI, while teams with AI did not differ significantly from teams without AI (p = 0.242, Table 2) and AI-aided solutions were more semantically similar to each other (Figure 13, p. 40, figure only).

authors_full: Anil R. Doshi, Oliver P. Hauser
title: Generative AI enhances individual creativity but reduces the collective diversity of novel content
pdf_filename: Doshi and Hauser (2024) - Generative AI Enhances Individual Creativity.pdf
one_line_finding: Relative to Human-only, access to up to five GPT-4 story ideas raised evaluator-rated novelty by 8.1 percent (b = 0.311, P < 0.001) and usefulness by 9.0 percent (b = 0.453, P < 0.001) (p. 3, Fig. 2A), while stories in both AI arms were more similar to the other stories in their condition (one idea b = 0.871, P < 0.001; five ideas b = 0.718, P = 0.003) (p. 4; Fig. 4B, p. 5).

authors_full: Guangrui Fan, Dandan Liu, Lihu Pan, Yishan Huang
title: Creative Momentum Transfer: How Timing and Labeling of AI Suggestions Shape Iterative Human Ideation
venue: Proceedings of the Thirty-Fourth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-25)
pdf_filename: Fan Liu Pan Huang (2025) - Creative Momentum Transfer.pdf
one_line_finding: Final expert-rated creativity was higher in Early-AI-Labeled (M = 6.01, SD = 0.48) than Control (M = 4.94), with an omnibus condition effect of F(4, 237) = 37.54, p < .001, partial eta-squared = .38 (PDF p. 4 (printed p. 10283), Section 4.1).

authors_full: Rosemary Fisher, Taylor Gogan, James Williams, Richard Laferriere, Gordon Campbell, Asanka Gunasekara, Jeremy Nguyen
title: Can ChatGPT enhance business student creativity? Evidence from a randomised controlled trial
pdf_filename: Fisher et al (2026) - Can ChatGPT enhance business student creativity.pdf
one_line_finding: ChatGPT-3.5 raised fluency (control 2.52 vs ChatGPT 3.65), originality (0.79 vs 1.14), and elaboration (0.80 vs 1.50) for Marketing students, raised fluency (1.78 vs 2.29) and elaboration (1.06 vs 1.99) but not originality (0.66 vs 0.77, p = .064) for Management students, and made no detectable difference for Entrepreneurship students (Tables 1-2, PDF p. 10).

authors_full: Philipp Gordetzki, Ivo Blohm, Melanie Clegg, Felix Schakols, Reto Hofstetter
title: Agency Configurations in Generative AI Ideation: How Textual and Visual Idea Concretizations Shape Idea Creativity and Ideator Effort
pdf_filename: Gordetzki et al (2026) - Agency Configurations in Generative AI Ideation.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 276 analyzed Prolific ideators (428 refinements), textual AI concretizations raised automated idea creativity by 0.29 SD over visual AI concretizations (Model 1a, SE 0.11) and by a reported, statistically significant 30% over the no-AI control (no coefficient printed), while visual versus control was 0.13 SD (SE 0.10, not significant) (PDF p. 9, article p. 8, Section 4.2 for the sample; PDF p. 10, article p. 9, Table 2 and Section 5).

authors_full: Jiaxuan Han, Ruqin Ren
title: Unequal AI Access Enhances Team Productivity through Negative Socio‐emotional Reactions and Cognitive Diversity
venue: Proceedings of the Association for Information Science and Technology
pdf_filename: Han and Ren (2025) - Why unequal AI access enhances team productivity.pdf
one_line_finding: Unequal AI access produced higher expert-rated press-release quality than full access (5.654 versus 5.250; t = 2.881, p < 0.01; p. 8, Section 4.1) and greater semantic distance between teammates’ spoken contributions (0.631 versus 0.510; t = 5.938, p < 0.01; p. 9, Section 4.2).

authors_full: Babak Hemmatian, Anita Keshmirian, Shravan Ramamoorthy, Maryam Jahadakbar, Eli Khuri-Reid, Jingtong Wang, Sarah Hadjarab, Sindre Veum, Pranav Gupta, Deepak Somaya, Lav Varshney
title: Two-Player Alternate Uses Test: A Controlled Testbed for Interactive Human-AI and Human-Human Co-Creation
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Creativity and Cognition (C&C '26, London, United Kingdom), ACM
pdf_filename: Hemmatian et al (2026) - Two-Player Alternate Uses Test.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 62 UIUC students, crowd-rated originality of Alternate Uses ideas from a 4-minute chat with a GPT-4 partner was statistically equivalent to that with a human partner (β_{GPT−HUM} = −0.11, SE = 0.13, 95% CI [−0.37, +0.16], p = .42; BF₀₁ = 10.95; p. 4, Section 4.1).

authors_full: Kartik Hosanagar, Daehwan Ahn
title: Designing Human and Generative AI Collaboration
pdf_filename: Hosanagar and Ahn (2025) - Designing Human and Generative AI Collaboration.pdf
one_line_finding: Human Creativity and Copilot exceeded Human Confirmation in adjusted overall story quality by 0.3376 (SE 0.106) and 0.3158 (SE 0.105), respectively (both p < 0.01; PDF p. 51, Table S7), while semantic similarity was 0.710, 0.743, and 0.779, respectively (PDF p. 7).

authors_full: Meiling Huang, Ming Jin, Ning Li
title: The Differential Role of Human Capital in Generative AI’s Impact on Creative Tasks
pdf_filename: Huang Jin Li (2025) - The Differential Role of Human Capital in Generative AIs Impact on Creative Task.pdf
one_line_finding: With GPT-4 available, flash-fiction novelty increased (b = 0.403, SE 0.19, p = .035; p. 19 and Table 2, p. 41), lyric novelty showed no clear difference (b = 0.087, SE 0.11; Table 4, p. 43), and the paper reported higher lyric-output similarity (cosine b = 0.014, p = .008; p. 29), with the between-person comparison basis unconfirmed.

authors_full: Shiyingzi Huang, Lirong Long, Yanghao Zhu, Julie N.Y. Zhu
title: Human–GenAI collaboration across creative phases: Cognitive mechanisms shaping novelty and usefulness
pdf_filename: Huang et al (2025) - HumanGenAI collaboration across creative phases.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 198 employees analyzed in Study 3, expert-rated novelty favors ChatGPT collaboration during idea generation and usefulness favors collaboration during elaboration (Table 3, p. 8: phase dummy 1 = elaboration, r = −0.30 and 0.42, respectively); the smaller Studies 2a and 2b report higher GenAI-condition novelty (6.05 vs 5.44; 42 analyzed; Table 1, p. 6) and usefulness (5.89 vs 5.49; 44 analyzed; Table 2, p. 7).

authors_full: Difang Huang, Shumin Yu, Fadong Chen, Weihua Zhou
title: The value of generative AI in creative teams depends on when it enters collective search
pdf_filename: Huang Yu Chen Zhou (2026) - The value of generative AI in creative teams depends on when it enters collectiv.pdf
one_line_finding: Divergent-stage AI and full-process AI improved human-rated team creativity versus no AI (4.86 and 4.81 vs 4.35; Hedges g=0.81, p=0.00265 and g=0.77, p=0.00424), while convergent-only and warning-framed AI showed no clear improvement (g=0.25, p=0.328 and g=0.43, p=0.104; Supplementary Table 5, PDF p. 31).

authors_full: Ziyang Huang, Jiajia Zhao, Xuan Fu
title: Generative AI as an External Cognitive Tool for Developing Creative Intelligence in Visual Design: A Mixed-Methods Randomized Study Using Cognitive Load Indicators and Motivational Modeling
pdf_filename: Huang Zhao Fu (2026) - Generative AI as an External Cognitive Tool for Developing Creative Intelligence.pdf
one_line_finding: Across 24 group projects, instruction integrating GenAI throughout design thinking had higher overall expert scores than traditional instruction with sporadic GenAI (86.58 [SD 1.84] vs 79.94 [SD 2.98]; t(22) = 6.57, p < 0.001, d = 2.68; p. 20, Section 4.6).

authors_full: Eaman Jahani, Benjamin S. Manning, Joe Zhang, Hong-Yi TuYe, Mohammed Alsobay, Christos Nicolaides, Siddharth Suri, David Holtz
title: Prompt Adaptation as a Dynamic Complement in Generative AI Systems
pdf_filename: Jahani et al (2026) - Prompt Adaptation as a Dynamic Complement in Generative AI Systems.pdf
one_line_finding: In the logo experiment (1,857 people analyzed; p. 47, Appendix C.5), DALL-E 3 (Verbatim) improved quality over DALL-E 2 by 0.8075 Bradley–Terry β (95% CI [0.7120, 0.9030], p < 10^−10; p. 18, section 4.2.1), with replay attributing approximately 92.7% to model capability and 7.2% to prompt adaptation (prompting p = 0.101; p. 19, section 4.2.2).

authors_full: Zheyu Jin, Junting Yin, Qiuyu Tian, Xinyan Zhou, Yangzhuo Li, Ting Yang, Junlong Luo
title: Can large language models teach creativity? Cognitive gains, affective gaps, and distinct neural patterns
venue: Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans
pdf_filename: Jin et al (2026) - Can large language models teach creativity.pdf
one_line_finding: After 8-10 minutes of ChatGPT-4.0 instruction, post-test AUT originality and flexibility on the trained item and flexibility on new items were higher than after human instruction or quiet rest (e.g., novel-item flexibility AI 9.67 ± 3.40, interaction F(2,92) = 7.182, p = 0.001; AI vs human p = 0.002, AI vs control p < 0.001), while no AI-versus-comparator post-test fluency difference is reported (pp. 5-6, Section 3.1; p. 6, Fig. 2).

authors_full: Yueqiao Jin, Roberto Martinez-Maldonado, Dragan Gašević, Xibin Han, Lixiang Yan
title: Emergent Learner Agency in Implicit Human–AI Collaboration: How Supportive and Contrarian AI Personas Reshape Interaction
pdf_filename: Jin et al (2026) - Emergent Learner Agency in Implicit HumanAI Collaboration.pdf
one_line_finding: Creative gains after supportive-AI, contrarian-AI, or human-only collaboration showed no significant condition difference (Kruskal-Wallis all p > .05, PDF p. 18; overall OLS F = 1.20, p = .310, R² = .029, PDF p. 19).

authors_full: Nathanael Jo, Manish Raghavan
title: Incentives shape how humans co-create with generative AI
venue: ICML 2026 Workshop on Human-AI Co-Creativity: Advances, Opportunities, and Challenges (non-archival report)
pdf_filename: Jo and Raghavan (2026) - Incentives shape how humans co-create with generative AI.pdf
one_line_finding: AI increased final-story MiniLM similarity by 0.043 under originality incentives and 0.062 under technical-quality incentives (both p < 0.01); originality incentives reduced similarity among AI users by 0.023 (p < 0.05), with variation across embedding models (p. 28, Table 5).

authors_full: Harang Ju, Sinan Aral
title: Collaborating with AI Agents: Field Experiments on Teamwork, Productivity, and Performance
pdf_filename: Ju and Aral (2026) - Collaborating with AI Agents.pdf
one_line_finding: Among the 2,234 analyzed participants, assignment to a GPT-4o agent teammate rather than a human teammate was associated with 1.954 more ads per person (SE 0.197; intercept 4.601), higher rated text quality (0.327, SE 0.024) and lower rated image quality (-0.133, SE 0.021) on 7-point scales, and less diverse ad copy among the 2,034 people analyzed for diversity (cosine distance to own-condition centroid -0.094, SE 0.006; intercept 0.303) (p. 22, Table 2).

authors_full: Taegon Kang, Kyungsoon Kim
title: The Effects of Generative AI Use on University Students’ Creative Idea Generation: Switching Effects in Repeated Task Performance
venue: The Journal of Korean Association of Computer Education
pdf_filename: Kang et al (2026) - The Effects of Generative AI Use on University Students' Creative Idea Generatio.pdf
one_line_finding: Students randomly given AI for the round-2 upgrade raised their 0-100 rubric creativity score by 28.63 points more than students kept without AI (SE 2.49, 95% CI [23.74, 33.52]; gains 37.73 vs 9.10), and students randomly cut off from AI gained 5.50 points less than those who kept it (SE 2.47, p = .026) (PDF pp. 7-8, Section 4.4.2; Table 4).

authors_full: Sean W. Kelley, David De Cremer, Christoph Riedl
title: Personalized AI Scaffolds Synergistic Multi-Turn Collaboration in Creative Work
pdf_filename: Kelley Cremer Riedl (2026) - Personalized AI Scaffolds Synergistic Multi-Turn Collaboration in Creative Work.pdf
one_line_finding: Personalized versus generic GPT-4o increased LLM-rated campaign quality (beta = 0.59, SE = 0.21, p = 0.005; PDF p. 6, Table S3 p. 59), while higher theme diversity was reported within the top quality tertile (beta = 20.5, SE = 6.5, p = 0.002; Fig. 2B p. 9), with no full-sample diversity contrast test printed.

authors_full: Nataliya Kosmyna, Eugene Hauptmann, Ye Tong Yuan, Jessica Situ, Xian-Hao Liao, Ashly Vivian Beresnitzky, Iris Braunstein, Pattie Maes
title: Your Brain on ChatGPT: Accumulation of Cognitive Debt when Using an AI Assistant for Essay Writing Task
pdf_filename: Kosmyna et al (2025) - Your Brain on ChatGPT.pdf
one_line_finding: The study analyzed 54 people (p. 22); its pooled named-entity figure reports higher consistency for LLM-labeled essays than Brain Only (p = 0.02898) or Search Engine (p = 0.00462), but the contributing sessions and test are unspecified (p. 59, Fig. 21).

authors_full: Harsh Kumar, Jonathan Vincentius, Ewan Jordan, Ashton Anderson
title: Human Creativity in the Age of LLMs: Randomized Experiments on Divergent and Convergent Thinking
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '25), Yokohama, Japan
pdf_filename: Kumar Vincentius Jordan Anderson (2025) - Human Creativity in the Age of LLMs.pdf
one_line_finding: After AI was removed, AUT originality was lower with prior GPT-4o strategies than with no AI (Kruskal-Wallis H(2) = 9.14, p = 0.010; Dunn p = 0.009) and did not differ with prior GPT-4o idea lists (p = 1.000) (p. 7), and RAT accuracy was lower with prior GPT-4o guidance than with no AI (Tukey p = 0.005; mean difference -10.6, 95% CI [-18.6, -2.7]) and did not differ with prior GPT-4o answers (p = 0.682) (p. 11).

authors_full: Clin K.Y. Lai, Simone A. Luchini, Nina Lauharatanahirun, Roger Beaty
title: Creative or uncreative partner: Comparing humans and AI in collaborative creative tasks
pdf_filename: Lai Luchini Lauharatanahirun Beaty (2025) - Creative or Uncreative Partner.pdf
one_line_finding: With a GPT-4o partner instead of a human partner, AUT originality scored over all pair responses, GPT-4o's included (2,970 responses, 2,066 without GPT-4o's), was higher (Human-Human minus Human-AI B = -0.065, SE 0.007), did not differ once word count, fluency, and item were controlled (B = 0.010, SE 0.008, p = .201), and was lower for the participants' own responses (B = 0.029, SE 0.010, p = .005; Table 2, pp. 9-10).

authors_full: Byung Cheol Lee, Jaeyeon (Jae) Chung
title: An empirical investigation of the impact of ChatGPT on creativity
pdf_filename: Lee and Chung (2024) - Empirical Investigation of ChatGPT on Creativity.pdf
one_line_finding: Across six online experiments, lay judges rated ideas produced with ChatGPT more creative than ideas produced with Google search (Cohen's d = 0.32 to 1.01) or with no aid (d = 0.56 in Experiment 2A, 1.88 in Experiment 2B) (Table 1, PDF p. 5, journal p. 1910).

authors_full: Ning Li, Huaikang Zhou, Kris Mikel-Hong
title: Generative AI Enhances Team Performance and Reduces Need for Traditional Teams
pdf_filename: Li Zhou Mikel-Hong (2024) - Generative AI Enhances Team Performance and Reduces Need for Traditional Teams.pdf
one_line_finding: AI-assisted teams scored higher on quality (0.417, SE 0.148) and novelty (0.344, SE 0.150), with a weaker usefulness gain (0.250, SE 0.150; p < .10) and no clear advantage from multiple AI touchpoints (pp. 37-39, Appendix B Tables 1-3).

authors_full: Haotian Liang, Dawei Zhang, Xianli An, Junjun Xu
title: Sequential Human-AI Collaboration Impairs Narrative Creativity in University Students: A Randomized Controlled Trial
pdf_filename: Liang Zhang An Xu (2026) - Sequential Human-AI Collaboration Impairs Narrative Creativity in University Stu.pdf
one_line_finding: Human-rated adjusted final-draft creativity was lower for AI-first (M = 4.86, d = -0.95, p = .002) and AI-follow (M = 4.81, d = -1.41, p < .001) than Human-only (M = 5.65), with no clear difference for AI-parallel (M = 5.17, d = -0.33, p = .262; p. 8, Section 3.2).

authors_full: Zhiwei Liu, Haode Zuo, Jue Feng, Yongjing Lu
title: Who Is the Best Helper for University Students' Mathematical Creativity? A Quasi‐Experimental Study of Human–ChatGPT, Human–Google, and Human–Human Co‐Creation
pdf_filename: Liu et al (2025) - Who Is the Best Helper for University Students' Mathematical Creativity.pdf
one_line_finding: Students working with ChatGPT scored higher than Google users and the peer arm on flexibility (15.03 vs 12.83 and 12.38) and fluency (27.85 vs 23.78 and 23.42), and between them on originality (5.47 vs 3.88 Google and 7.00 peer); three-group F (2, 172) = 9.71, 7.91, and 18.31, Bonferroni p ≤ 0.001, with no pairwise test printed (p. 7, Table 3).

authors_full: Xin Liu, Yi Wen, Xiaozhe Yang, Yihe Gao
title: Generative AI-Supported Creative Writing Among Primary School Students: A Study of Creative Writing Performance, Writing Self-Efficacy, and Flow State
pdf_filename: Liu et al (2026) - Generative AI Supported Creative Writing Among Primary School Students.pdf
one_line_finding: Fifth graders who wrote with Deepseek scored 88.850 (SD 1.420, n = 20) on a researcher-rated 100-point creative writing rubric, against 86.825 (SD 2.719, n = 38) for students writing in pairs and 85.133 (SD 2.120, n = 20) for students writing alone (one-way ANOVA F = 13.095, p = 0.000***; LSD a > b, a > c), p. 7, Table 1.

authors_full: Chenghai Liu, Jiayao Guo, Rongxia Gao, Xiangnan Chen, Qiuhan Zhu, Pengcheng Chang
title: Borrowed or kept? How self-generation-first and direct-adoption AI workflows shape immediate unaided reasoning
pdf_filename: Liu et al (2026) - Borrowed or kept.pdf
one_line_finding: On the unaided essay 15-20 minutes later, direct-adoption AI reduced reasoning quality (-0.38, d = -0.28) and within-essay flexibility (-0.30, d = -0.23) versus No-AI, but not originality (q = 0.28); self-generation-first did not fall below No-AI (pp. 7-8, Section 3.4).

authors_full: Zhiwei Liu, Gang Li, Haode Zuo, Yongjing Lu, Jue Feng
title: Exploring the impact of ChatGPT on college students’ mathematical creativity: A quasi-experimental study
pdf_filename: Liu Zuo Feng Lu (2026) - Exploring the impact of ChatGPT on college students' mathematical creativity.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 124 analyzed students, the ChatGPT group scored higher than controls on mathematical flexibility (d = 0.73), fluency (d = 0.66) and originality (d = 0.42) (PDF p. 11, printed p. 49, Table 5; sample size: PDF p. 7, printed p. 45, Participants).

authors_full: Houjiang Liu, Yujin Choi, Sanjana Gautam, Gabriel Jaffe, Soo Young Rieh, Matthew Lease
title: Who Owns Creativity and Who Does the Work? Trade-offs in LLM-Supported Research Ideation
pdf_filename: Liu et al (2026) - Who Owns Creativity and Who Does the Work.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 51 analyzed researchers, unique proposals per hour did not differ significantly across Intensive, Medium, and Low control: means 1.58, 1.88, and 2.19, respectively; F(2, 48) = 1.52, p = 0.22 (p. 14, Table 4; analyzed counts on p. 13, Section 5.3.1).

authors_full: Simone A. Luchini, Jimmy Pronchick, Simon M. Ceh, James C. Kaufman, Dan Richard Johnson, Janet Rafner, Roger E. Beaty
title: The Roles of Idea Generation and Elaboration in Human-AI Collaborative Creativity
pdf_filename: Luchini et al (2025) - The Roles of Idea Generation and Elaboration in Human-AI Collaborative Creativit.pdf
one_line_finding: Within person, stories written with GPT-3.5 available scored higher on MAoSS originality (M = .56 vs .52; t(262) = 5.56, p < .001, d = .34; p. 14) and contributed less to semantic diversity (t(262) = -1.99, p = .047, d = -.123; p. 17) than the same 263 analyzed students' stories written without AI (Figure 2, p. 15).

authors_full: Nguyễn Thị Mai
title: Generative AI and Student Creativity: Cognitive Scaffolding Tool or Constraint on Originality? An Empirical Investigation in Vietnamese Higher Education
venue: International Conference on Creativity, Management, Education, Technology and Sciences Conference 2026 Proceedings
pdf_filename: Mai (2026) - Generative AI and Student Creativity.pdf
one_line_finding: Unconstrained AI raised fluency (11.45 vs 5.12) but lowered originality (3.41 vs 4.82) and diversity (cosine similarity 0.689 vs 0.412), while scaffolding raised originality (5.44; reported d = 0.61 vs control) and overall creativity (5.51 vs 4.48; PDF pp. 6-7, Tables 1-2).

authors_full: Sebastian Maier, Manuel Schneider, Stefan Feuerriegel
title: Partnering with Generative AI: Experimental Evaluation of Model-Led and Human-Led Interaction in Human-AI Co-Creation
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '26), Barcelona, Spain, April 13-17, 2026
pdf_filename: Maier Schneider Feuerriegel (2026) - Partnering with Generative AI.pdf
one_line_finding: In Study 1 (486 analyzed), expert-rated idea quality rose over the no-AI control with model-led rewriting (3.11 vs 2.68, t(481) = 3.86, d = 0.55) and question-mode (2.96, t(481) = 2.49, d = 0.36) but not with vanilla GPT-4.1 chat (2.70, d = 0.02) or suggestion-mode (2.78, d = 0.13), and question-mode ideas were more diverse than model-led ideas (0.379 vs 0.309, d = 0.76; no AI-versus-control diversity test) (p. 12, Tables 2-3).

authors_short: McGuire, De Cremer, and Van de Cruys
authors_full: Jack McGuire, David De Cremer, Tim Van de Cruys
title: Establishing the importance of co-creation and self-efficacy in creative collaboration with artificial intelligence
pdf_filename: McGuire Cremer Van de Cruys (2024) - Establishing the importance of co-creation and self-efficacy in creative collabo.pdf
one_line_finding: Professional poets rated poems submitted by people who received an AI-generated poem to edit as less creative than poems written alone (Study 1: 12.55 vs 18.23 on a 1 to 40 scale, p < 0.001, p. 4 and Table 1; Study 2: 12.53 vs 15.74, p = 0.001, p. 6 and Table 2 on p. 7), while writing line by line in turns with the AI did not differ from writing alone (14.70 vs 15.74, p = 0.278) and scored higher than the editing condition (p = 0.026).

authors_full: Peidong Mei, Deborah N. Brewis, Fortune Nwaiwu, Deshan Sumanathilaka, Fernando Alva-Manchego, Joanna Demaree-Cotton
title: If ChatGPT can do it, where is my creativity? generative AI boosts performance but diminishes experience in creative writing
venue: Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans
pdf_filename: Mei et al (2025) - If ChatGPT can do it, where is my creativity.pdf
one_line_finding: In an online experiment that randomly assigned UK university students to use or not use ChatGPT on a 10-minute task listing uses for a 'printer that can print anything in 2097' (225 analyzed), the AI arm's mean counts of uses and of conceptual domains were above Control's in all four subgroups (Fig. 2, p. 6), with no significant difference in frequency in Group 2 (b = 0.91, SE = 2.30, p = .69) or on either count in Group 4 (p. 6), and the AI condition's pooled outputs scored higher on group-level frequency (635 vs 552) and flexibility (442 vs 313) (Fig. 5, p. 9); pooled regressions are only in SI Table 3, not in this PDF.

authors_full: Lennart Meincke, Gideon Nave, Christian Terwiesch
title: ChatGPT decreases idea diversity in brainstorming
pdf_filename: Meincke et al (2025) - ChatGPT Decreases Idea Diversity in Brainstorming.pdf
one_line_finding: In a reanalysis of Lee and Chung's (2024) experiments, ChatGPT-aided idea pools had a lower fraction of unique ideas (Universal Sentence Encoder cosine threshold 0.8) than comparison pools in every experiment, for example 0.74 vs 0.96 with web search (Experiment 1), 0.70 vs 0.92 unaided and 0.91 with web search (Experiment 2a), and 0.41 vs 1.00 unaided (Experiment 2b); the paper reports the difference as significant in four of five experiments, all but Experiment 4 (p. 1108, Fig. 1 and text).

authors_full: Shiri Melumad, Jin Ho Yun
title: Experimental evidence of the effects of large language models versus web search on depth of learning
pdf_filename: Melumad and Yun (2025) - Experimental evidence of the effects of large language models versus web search.pdf
one_line_finding: Advice following LLM learning was more similar across writers than advice following web-link learning (cosine similarity 0.159 vs 0.057, 0.224 vs 0.072, and 0.214 vs 0.073 in Experiments 1-3; all P < 0.001; pp. 5-7) and was rated less helpful by recipients (3.553 vs 3.816; P < 0.001; p. 8).

authors_full: Lucas Memmert, Eva Bittner
title: Human-AI Collaboration for Brainstorming: Effect of the Presence of AI Ideas on Breadth of Exploration
venue: Proceedings of the 57th Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences
pdf_filename: Memmert and Bittner (2024) - Human-AI Collaboration for Brainstorming.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 52 analyzed students, lists including accepted AI suggestions covered a median of 5 categories versus 2 without AI (U=546.5, p<.001, rank-biserial rB=.617), while human-origin category coverage showed no significant difference (U=326.0, p=.830; PDF p. 5, section 4; p. 6, section 4.1).

authors_full: Lucas Memmert, Izabel Cvetkovic, Navid Tavanapour, Eva Bittner
title: Brainstorming with a Generative Language Model: Effect of Exposure to AI Ideas on Brainstorming Performance and Cognitive Load
pdf_filename: Memmert et al (2025) - Brainstorming with a Generative Language Model.pdf
one_line_finding: With on-demand GPT-3.5 ideas, participants' final idea lists (own plus copied GLM ideas) were longer (mdn 7 vs 5; U = 963.5, p = 0.006) and covered more categories (mdn 5 vs 3; U = 1080.0, p < 0.001), and their shortlists were rated more novel (mean 3.396 vs 2.876; t(73) = 2.889, p = 0.005, d = 0.667) and more valuable (mdn 4.900 vs 4.425; U = 994.0, p = 0.002), but they wrote fewer ideas themselves (mdn 4 vs 5; U = 475.0, text p = 0.015; Fig. 7a instead marks **, defined as p < .01) and their own ideas were not rated more novel (U = 699.5, p = 0.406) or valuable (U = 737.5, p = 0.204) (PDF pp. 12-13, Sects. 4.1-4.2, Figs. 7-8).

authors_full: Shakked Noy, Whitney Zhang
title: Experimental evidence on the productivity effects of generative artificial intelligence
pdf_filename: Noy and Zhang (2023) - Experimental evidence on the productivity effects of generative artificial intel.pdf
one_line_finding: ChatGPT assignment raised average writing grades by 0.45 SD in the text (p<0.001; p. 4) and 0.41 SD in Fig. 1B (95% CI [0.23, 0.59]; p. 12), while originality was reported to increase without a separate numerical estimate (p. 4).

authors_full: Min Jae Park
title: AI as a cognitive collaborator: Assimilation and accommodation in human–machine teaming for innovation
pdf_filename: Park (2026) - AI as a cognitive collaborator.pdf
one_line_finding: Among analyzed individual participants (90 with GPT-4, 92 without AI), the AI arm had higher expert-rated solution novelty (7.1 vs 5.8) and quality (7.3 vs 6.2) on 10-point scales (p. 6, Table 2; p. 5, Measures).

authors_full: Peinuan Qin, Chi-Lan Yang, Jingshu Li, Jing Wen, Yi-Chieh Lee
title: Timing Matters: How Using LLMs at Different Timings Influences Writers' Perceptions and Ideation Outcomes in AI-Assisted Ideation
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '25), Yokohama, Japan, ACM
pdf_filename: Qin et al (2025) - Timing Matters.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 60 Prolific participants, randomized and analyzed 30 per arm, unlocking GPT-4 only after independent ideation (C_after) rather than from the start (C_before) gave lower TF-IDF similarity to the LLM's ideas (0.648 vs 0.899; p = 0.006, d = 0.747; the printed t = 4.778 is inconsistent) and no clear difference in the number of ideas (5.567 vs 3.867; t(58) = -1.897, p = 0.063, d = -0.490, which the paper calls marginal) or in within-person idea diversity (t(36.472) = 1.337, p = 0.189) (p. 7, Section 4.1; p. 8, Figure 3).

authors_full: Jude Abishek Rayan, Shaokang Jiang, Nishant Balaji, Jinmao Wang, Ian Gross, Cole Biehle, Steven P. Dow
title: Cueing the Crowd: LLM-Driven Conversational Cues Across Different Meeting Modalities Increase Topical Diversity of Generated Ideas
venue: CI '25: Proceedings of the ACM Collective Intelligence Conference (San Diego, CA, USA, August 4-6, 2025)
pdf_filename: Rayan et al (2025) - Cueing the Crowd.pdf
one_line_finding: Dyads that received GPT-4o-mini cues produced ideas with higher topic diversity (entropy 2.3, SD 0.3 vs 2.1, SD 0.4; F(1, 67.03) = 6.51, p = 0.013) and conversations covering more topics (9.6 vs 8.0 unique topics; F(1, 50.76) = 6.25, p = 0.016), with no significant difference in the number of ideas and no printed test of across-group homogenization (PDF pp. 7-9, Sec. 5.1, Fig. 5; PDF p. 17, Fig. 6).

authors_full: Alon Rosenbaum, Yigal David, Eran Kaufman, Gilad Ravid, Amit Ronen, Assaf Krebs
title: Scaffolding Creativity: How Divergent and Convergent LLM Personas Shape Human Machine Creative Problem-Solving
pdf_filename: Rosenbaum et al (2025) - Scaffolding Creativity.pdf
one_line_finding: Persona-guided ChatGPT increased between-person semantic distance versus standard ChatGPT (M=0.34 vs 0.28; p=2.20 × 10−6), with no significant fluency difference (M=8.55 vs 9.23) or within-person distance difference (M=0.59 vs 0.59; p=.90; pp. 9-10, section 5.3 and Figure 6).

authors_full: Paul Röttger, Kobi Hackenburg, Hannah Rose Kirk, Christopher Summerfield
title: Measuring and Mitigating Persona Distortions from AI Writing Assistance
pdf_filename: Rottger Hackenburg Kirk Summerfield (2026) - Measuring and Mitigating Persona Distortions from AI Writing Assistance.pdf
one_line_finding: In the fixed-order comparison, AI-assisted paragraphs were rated +12.5 points more original (p. 5, Figure 2B) and showed lower dispersion on 22 of 29 attributes (p. 4, Section 2.2), while randomized reranking attenuated the AI-induced clarity increase by 26.9% (p. 8, Figure 4D).

authors_full: Vanessa Sattele, Juan Carlos Ortiz
title: Sketching vs. AI Prompt Based Design Intent Evolution in Undergraduate Students: an Exploratory Study
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '26), Barcelona, Spain
pdf_filename: Sattele et al (2026) - Sketching vs AI Prompt Based Design Intent Evolution in Undergraduate Students.pdf
one_line_finding: Expert creativity ratings of image-level ideas averaged 2.89 in the AI groups vs 2.52 in the sketch groups (44 vs 71 ideas, no test; Table 1, p. 6), but the two reported t-tests give mixed results (t(76) = -3.995, p < .001 and t(34.8) = 1.039, p = .306; p. 6), and AI students produced more total ideas (9.7 vs 2.8 per participant) but fewer image-level ideas (1.4 vs 2.2), with 18 of 30 converging on one light-ring concept (pp. 6-7).

authors_full: Farhana Shahid, Maximilian Dittgen, Mor Naaman, Aditya Vashistha
title: Examining Human-AI Collaboration for Co-Writing Constructive Comments Online
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
pdf_filename: Shahid Dittgen Naaman Vashistha (2025) - Examining Human-AI Collaboration for Co-Writing Constructive Comments Online.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 103 analyzed writers (pp. 2, 12), AI-assisted comments showed no significant semantic-similarity difference (0.42 vs. 0.41) but lower ROUGE-L overlap (0.16 vs. 0.18; U=42029, p<0.001, r=0.16; p. 18, Table 8), and were preferred as more constructive in 64% of paired judgments (p. 15, Figure 4).

authors_full: Joongi Shin, Anna Polyanskaya, Andrés Lucero, Antti Oulasvirta
title: No Evidence for LLMs Being Useful in Problem Reframing
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '25), Yokohama, Japan, ACM
pdf_filename: Shin et al (2025) - No Evidence for LLMs Being Useful in Problem Reframing.pdf
one_line_finding: Of 456 designers randomized to reframe a design problem without an LLM or with GPT-4o in three ways, 280 were analyzed, and rater-scored novelty and usefulness of the frame each person picked as best did not differ between MANUAL (62 analyzed) and LLM-ALL (218 analyzed) or among the four approaches (all p > 0.05), reported only as box plots (p. 6, Figure 4 and Section 4.2; p. 8, Figure 5; pp. 8-9, Section 5.2).

authors_full: Fenglin Song, Biao Xu
title: Effects of integrating a structured design thinking strategy into generative AI-supported design learning on students’ design achievement, creative self-efficacy, and problem-solving skills
pdf_filename: Song and Xu (2026) - Effects of integrating a structured design thinking strategy into generative AI.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 120 analyzed students, mean design-achievement scores were 20.90 with structured design thinking plus AI, 18.65 with free AI use, and 16.13 with traditional learning; all pairwise p < 0.001 are reported (p. 9, Table 1 and section 4.1).

authors_full: Nathan Sorin, Margherita Pagani
title: The role of task breadth and cognitive flexibility in generative AI-supported creative idea generation
pdf_filename: Sorin et al (2026) - The role of task breadth and cognitive flexibility in generative AI-supported cr.pdf
one_line_finding: Seeing GPT-3-generated startup ideas raised breadth of exploration in the broad Study 1 task (2.32 vs 1.60 categories, d = 0.67, Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.01; p. 8, Section 4.6.1; Table 4, p. 9) and lowered similarity among participants' first ideas (0.74 vs 0.81, permutation p = 0.00; Table 7, p. 11), but showed no statistically significant difference in either in the narrow Study 2 EdTech task (breadth 1.39 vs 1.38, p = 1.00, p. 10, Section 5.5.1; Table 6; similarity 0.87 vs 0.87, p = 0.09, Table 7; p. 11); untested expert creativity means were 4.23 vs 4.35 in Study 1 and 4.86 vs 4.52 in Study 2 (Appendix D, p. 18).

authors_full: Xiaotian Su, Laura Rimell, Jiazheng Li, Amal Rannen-Triki, Ulrich Paquet, Lisa Anne Hendricks, Rida Qadri, Daphne Ippolito, Piotr Mirowski
title: Who Thinks First? Designing Productive Friction with Engage-to-Unlock GenAI
pdf_filename: Su et al (2026) - Who Thinks First.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 398 analyzed writers, essay semantic dispersion was descriptively similar across conditions (Human-Only 0.179, Engage-to-Unlock 0.187, Standard Chatbot 0.188, Time-Matched Unlock 0.188), without a formal between-condition test (p. 6, section 3.2; p. 13, Table 1; p. 9, section 3.5.3).

authors_full: Shuhua Sun, Zhuyi Angelina Li, Maw-Der Foo, Jing Zhou, Jackson G. Lu
title: How and for whom using generative AI affects creativity: A field experiment.
pdf_filename: Sun et al (2025) - How and for whom using generative AI affects creativity.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 250 analyzed employees, ChatGPT access increased supervisor-rated creativity (d = 1.25) and written-response novelty (d = 0.35), while usefulness favored AI in the unadjusted comparison (d = 0.33) but was not significant with controls (p = .136; PDF pp. 6, 8, 10, Results and Tables 2–3).

authors_full: Marek Urban, Filip Děchtěrenko, Jiří Lukavský, Veronika Hrabalová, Filip Svacha, Cyril Brom, Kamila Urban
title: ChatGPT improves creative problem-solving performance in university students: An experimental study
pdf_filename: Urban et al (2024) - ChatGPT improves creative problem-solving performance in university students.pdf
one_line_finding: Students randomly assigned to solve the Product Improvement Task with ChatGPT received higher expert ratings than students without it on quality (3.60 vs 2.99, d = 0.69), elaboration (2.79 vs 2.21, d = 0.61), and originality (2.74 vs 2.21, d = 0.55), all p < .001 (77 vs 68 students analyzed; means, d, and p in Table 2, p. 16; Ns in Table 1, p. 11).

authors_full: A. Villarreal, A. Sachdeva, L. Brandimarte
title: LLM Randomness and Creativity: An Experiment on Human-AI Collaboration
venue: 2026 49th MIPRO ICT and Electronics Convention (MIPRO), Opatija, Croatia
pdf_filename: Villarreal et al (2026) - LLM Randomness and Creativity.pdf
one_line_finding: Neither LLM temperature nor AI availability changed AUT semantic distance (HighRandomness -0.008, SE 0.037; NoAI -0.002, SE 0.044; Table II, PDF p. 4) or DAT scores (not significant and not reported, PDF p. 3), and Table III shows no significant condition coefficient for RAT accuracy after controlling for AI use (HighRandomness -0.074, SE 0.049; NoAI -0.044, SE 0.055; PDF p. 5), though the Discussion reports that AI availability raised RAT accuracy from 45 to 55 percent (p < .05, PDF p. 3).

authors_full: Samangi Wadinambiarachchi, Ryan M. Kelly, Saumya Pareek, Qiushi Zhou, Eduardo Velloso
title: The Effects of Generative AI on Design Fixation and Divergent Thinking
venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '24), Honolulu, HI, USA, May 11-16, 2024, ACM
pdf_filename: Wadinambiarachchi et al (2024) - The Effects of Generative AI on Design Fixation and Divergent Thinking.pdf
one_line_finding: Compared with no support, Midjourney access raised the design fixation score (probit posterior mean .32, SD 0.13, 89% CI [.11, .54]; Table 1, p. 8) and lowered originality by an amount the authors call negligible (-.03, SD .02, 89% CI [-.06, -.01]; Table 4, p. 10), while the fluency (-.21, [-.66, .26]) and variety (-.29, [-.74, .17]) estimates have 89% intervals that include zero (Tables 2-3, p. 9).

authors_full: Yun Wan, Yoram M. Kalman
title: Diverse AI personas can mitigate the homogenization effect in human-AI collaborative ideation
venue: Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans
pdf_filename: Wan and Kalman (2026) - Diverse AI personas can mitigate the homogenization effect in human-AI collabora.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 97 analyzed UK Prolific writers (100 randomized), optional access to plot ideas from 10 GPT-4o personas did not raise story similarity: similarity to the condition centroid was 90.588 (no AI), 90.095 (1-plot) and 90.233 (5-plot), F(2, 94) = 0.573, p = 0.57 (Tables 2-3, pp. 12-13), and pairwise similarity was lower, that is diversity higher, in the 1-plot arm (-1.073, 95% CI [-1.971, -0.175], p = 0.019) but not significantly in the 5-plot arm (-0.488, p = 0.291) (Table 4, p. 14).

authors_full: Sarah Shi Hui Wong, Sophia Xuefei Qiu
title: Think First, ChatGPT Later: Guiding Human–AI Collaboration for Learning Gains in Independent Human Creativity
pdf_filename: Wong and Qiu (2026) - Think First, ChatGPT Later.pdf
one_line_finding: With ChatGPT available, free use raised expert-rated originality over no AI (4.08 vs 3.06, d = 0.79, p < .001) while guided 'think first, ChatGPT later' use did not (3.30, d = 0.18, p = .90); on the next task, done without AI in the same session, free users matched the no-AI group (2.69 vs 2.63, d = 0.04) and the guided group scored higher than both (3.42; d = 0.52 vs no AI, d = 0.48 vs free use) (p. 20, Fig. 2A on p. 21).

authors_full: Xuekang Wu, Guy Aridor, Artem Timoshenko
title: Guided Creativity: AI Intermediation for Enhancing Originality and Quality in Visual Design
venue: Working paper (SSRN 5371575; revision posted on author website)
pdf_filename: Wu et al (2025) - Guided Creativity.pdf
one_line_finding: In the main logo contest (292 analyzed designers), AI variations increased mean click-attractiveness quality versus Blind (beta_Var - beta_Blind = 0.0665, SE 0.0197) and top-50 submission originality versus human exemplars (beta_Open - beta_Var = -0.0139, SE 0.0053), with no clear quality difference versus human exemplars or originality difference versus Blind, and the restaurant replication (208 analyzed) showed the same direction pattern (PDF pp. 20 and 29, Tables 1-2; PDF p. 64, Tables WA-C.3/WA-C.4; PDF pp. 68-69, Tables WA-D.4/WA-D.5).

authors_full: Sarah H. Wu, Yuewen Yang, Angela Y. Lee, Alex Liebscher, Kristina Rapuano, Kate Niederhoffer, Jeffrey T. Hancock
title: The Role of Human Agency in Human-AI Co-Creativity
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Creativity and Cognition (C&C '26), London, United Kingdom, ACM
pdf_filename: Wu et al (2026) - The Role of Human Agency in Human-AI Co-Creativity.pdf
one_line_finding: Evaluator ratings of creativity and originality did not differ significantly by condition (ps > .60, p. 15; Table A2, p. 35), high-agency ideas were less similar to their condition-object centroid than low-agency ideas (cosine similarity -0.050, SE 0.021, Table A3, p. 36; Tukey t(125) = -2.45, p < .05, p. 16), and low-agency ideas formed fewer clusters, had a lower noise ratio, and had more unequal cluster sizes than control ideas (permutation p = .04, .02, and .005, p. 17).

authors_full: Nety Wu, Hyunjin Kim, Chengyi Lin
title: More Ideas, Less Strategic Focus: How AI Changes the Alternatives Decision-Makers Consider
pdf_filename: Wu Kim Lin (2025) - More Ideas, Less Strategic Focus.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 305 analyzed MBA students, GPT-4 raised option counts by 1.55 (SE 0.43) with full access and 2.68 (SE 0.55) with ideation-onward access, while full access lowered the strategic share by 0.07 (SE 0.03) and strategic selection by 0.15 (SE 0.07), with no clear partial-access effect on either strategic outcome (PDF p. 38, Table 2).

authors_full: Lixiang Yan, Xibin Han, Yu Zhang, Samuel Greiff, Inge Molenaar, Roberto Martinez-Maldonado, Yizhou Fan, Linxuan Zhao, Xinyu Li, Yueqiao Jin, Dragan Gašević
title: The Social Blindspot in Human-AI Collaboration: How Undetected AI Personas Reshape Team Dynamics
pdf_filename: Yan et al (2025) - The Social Blindspot in Human-AI Collaboration.pdf
one_line_finding: Following the discussion, creative-writing gains showed no clear advantage from AI teammates: H2_S versus H3 beta = 0.336, CR2 SE = 0.184, p = .074, Holm p = 1.00; the other creative AI-versus-H3 contrasts also had Holm p = 1.00 (p. 52, Table 28).

authors_full: Fang Yuan, Chunlei Liu, Jiaqin Yang
title: The Impact of Generative AI Dependence on University Students’ Creativity: The Mediating Role of Critical Thinking and the Moderating Role of Thinking Orientation
pdf_filename: Yuan et al (2026) - The Impact of Generative AI Dependence on University Students' Creativity.pdf
one_line_finding: In Study 2, students randomly told to adopt ChatGPT's AUT solutions directly scored lower on rater-scored creativity than students told to use ChatGPT only as a supplementary reference (4.78 vs 5.20, t(130) = 4.03, p < 0.001, d = 0.70; p. 6, Table 2), and in Study 3 students assigned to high AI dependence through a trust-game instruction scored lower under both thinking-orientation primes (Table 4, Model 2: B = -1.35, SE = 0.09; cell means 2.99 vs 4.52 outcome-oriented and 4.40 vs 5.55 process-oriented; p. 9).

authors_full: Man ZHANG, Yang PENG, Yajie WANG, Huiqing HU, Shi CHEN, Qingbai ZHAO
title: Perspective taking shapes creative performance in human-AI collaboration
pdf_filename: Zhang et al (2026) - Perspective taking shapes creative performance in human-AI collaboration.pdf
one_line_finding: Humans collaborating with GPT-5-mini generated more novel ideas than humans collaborating with another person in AUT (d = 0.47, p = 0.029; p. 17, section 3.2.2) and PIT (d = 0.42, p = 0.045; p. 22, section 3.3.2).

authors_full: Chu Zhang, XiaoKe Zeng, Jin Zhang, Ruoyu Wen, Vince Siu, Richard William Allen, Ray LC
title: FIERO: Empowering Creative Writing Through Collaborative Game Play
pdf_filename: Zhang et al (2026) - FIERO.pdf
one_line_finding: Creativity judgments of FIERO's bundled card-game/AI condition differed by evaluator (net advantage: Claude -27.2%, Gemini 50.6%, GPT-5.2 -7.4%), while overall-preference net advantages favored FIERO (45.7-65.4%; p. 29, Figure 14).

authors_full: Jiexin Zheng, Ka Chau Wong, Jiali Zhou, Tat Koon Koh
title: Large Language Model in Ideation for Product Innovation: An Exploratory Comparative Study
pdf_filename: Zheng Wong Zhou Koh (2024) - Large Language Model in Ideation for Product Innovation.pdf
one_line_finding: Compared with participants assigned to Google Search, those assigned to ChatGPT submitted more valid ideas (3.533 vs 1.533, F = 27.65), ideas rated more novel (z-scores 0.010 vs -0.057, F = 4.88, p < 0.05) but less functionally appropriate (0.055 vs 0.213, F = 10.77, p < 0.01), and ideas more semantically divergent within their condition (0.134 vs 0.123, F = 25.68, p < 0.01) (Table 3, p. 20).

authors_full: Wang Zhou, YeaJin Kim
title: Long-term impact of ChatGPT-4 on music students' creative and analytical skills: A follow-up study
pdf_filename: Zhou et al (2026) - Long-term impact of ChatGPT-4 on music students' creative and analytical skills.pdf
one_line_finding: Among 74 music students analyzed in a study reporting class-level random assignment, the ChatGPT-4 group had higher adjusted expert-rated creativity than the traditional-instruction group (4.71 vs 4.35; F(1, 69) = 7.216, p = .009, η² = .096; p. 12, Tables 5-6) and a steeper reported creativity growth slope (0.315 vs 0.210; p. 9, Table 3).

authors_full: Yiyong Zhou, Qinghan Liu, Jihao Huang, Guiquan Li
title: Creative scar without generative AI: Individual creativity fails to sustain while homogeneity keeps climbing
pdf_filename: Liu et al (2024) - When ChatGPT is Gone Creativity Reverts and Homogeneity Persists.pdf
one_line_finding: With ChatGPT on Days 2 to 6, the treatment group scored higher on AUT novelty (Day 6: 39.84 vs 14.80; t = -4.84, P 0.000; Table 2a p. 8, Table 1 p. 11) and on the expert rating of solution novelty ('Creativity' in Table 2b), but not on Day 7 without ChatGPT (AUT novelty 17.60 vs 13.02, P 0.053; solution novelty P 0.122; Tables 2a and 2b p. 8, Table 1 pp. 11-12), while its AUT answers stayed more similar at Day 30 (SBERT 0.39 vs 0.33, p ≤ .001; p. 14, Table 3 p. 16).

authors_full: Zhihao Zhou, Letao Xiao, Jiayi Wang, Shuai Tong, Wenyu Zhang, Ning Hao
title: Group-AI Collaboration Enhances Creativity Performance: The Roles of Perspective-Taking and AI Utilisation Strategies
pdf_filename: Zhou et al (2026) - Group AI Collaboration Enhances Creativity Performance.pdf
one_line_finding: Pairs in which each member had ChatGPT-4o produced ideas that two LLM judges rated more useful than human-only pairs (M = 4.09 vs 3.24; β = 0.84, SE = 0.04) and than people working alone with ChatGPT-4o (3.34; β = 0.74, SE = 0.06), and more original (3.68 vs 2.74 and 2.70; β = 0.94, SE = 0.05 and β = 0.98, SE = 0.07), while fluency did not differ and working alone with AI did not differ from human-only pairs (p > 0.05) (pp. 15-16, Section 3.1; p. 17, Figure 3).

authors_full: Feng Zhu, Wenbo Zou
title: Generative AI adoption in human creative tasks: Experimental evidence
pdf_filename: Zhu and Zou (2026) - Generative AI Adoption in Human Creative Tasks.pdf
one_line_finding: Access to ChatGPT 3.5 raised the image-text creativity grade of students' picture ideas by 0.24 points on a 1-10 scale (0.32 SDs, SE 0.062, p < .01; control mean 5.93) relative to working alone (p. 7; Table 3 col 2, p. 8), while the text-only effect was 0.090 (SE 0.094) and not significant.
